ca.title: Install the Portunus certificate on devices
ca.lead: sing-box profiles and subscriptions already trust it. For other apps, install the certificate authority once per device: server certificates it issues renew by themselves.
ca.qr: Scan with the phone to download
ca.qrOff: A code for the phone appears once subscriptions are on: set their port in Settings.
ca.iosSteps:
Download the certificate on the iPhone or iPad: scan the code or open the file.
Open Settings and tap Profile Downloaded at the top.
Tap Install and enter the device passcode.
Go to Settings, General, About, Certificate Trust Settings.
Turn on full trust for the certificate: its name is shown above.
ca.androidSteps:
Download the certificate on the phone: scan the code or open the file.
Open Settings and go to Security.
Open Encryption & credentials (on some phones: More security settings).
Tap Install a certificate and choose CA certificate.
Confirm the warning and pick the downloaded file.
ca.androidNote: Apps built on sing-box (Hiddify, NekoBox) ignore certificates installed by the user: give them the subscription or the regular link instead.
ca.windowsSteps:
Download the .cer file and open it.
Click Install Certificate.
Choose Local Machine and confirm.
Select Place all certificates in the following store and click Browse.
Choose Trusted Root Certification Authorities and finish the wizard.
ca.macosSteps:
Download the .crt file and open it: Keychain Access starts.
Add the certificate to the System keychain.
Find the certificate in the list by the name shown above and open it with a double click.
Expand Trust and set When using this certificate to Always Trust.
Close the window and enter your password.
ca.fingerprintHint: The device shows it before installing: it must match.

Run this once on the main server, in the folder with docker-compose.yml: it replaces that file with the current one and starts the updater. logs.hint.refused: {address} refused the connection: nothing listens on that port there. Usually this is the site's side, not the server's.

logs.hint.noHost: The name {address} does not exist, or the server's DNS did not answer.
logs.hint.stranger: Someone knocked who is not a client of yours: a scanner, or an app with an old link. Nothing to do unless it is your own device.

access.title: Opening the panel
access.description: By default the panel is reached through an SSH tunnel only. With a domain it can also be opened in a browser directly, over HTTPS.
access.needsDomain: Give the server a domain above first: a certificate cannot be issued for an IP address.
access.enableHint: Only by a secret address, shown below. Everybody else sees an ordinary site instead.
access.acmeHint: Recommended. Free, obtained and renewed by the panel itself, on port 443. A VLESS connection can use the same port.
access.ownHint: Paste the certificate and its key. Any port can be used.
access.portHint: A TCP port no connection uses.
access.certificateHint: In PEM form, with the chain of intermediates after it.
access.certificateKeep: One is stored. Leave both fields empty to keep it.
access.addressHint: Save it: this is how the panel is opened. {origin} alone shows the cover site.
access.decoyHint: What a stranger sees at your domain instead of the panel. Leave it empty: the panel then shows a small ordinary site it has made itself, different for every installation. Or give the address of another site to show as if it lived here.
access.shared: Port {port} is shared with a VLESS connection: its clients are served by it, and browsers are passed on to the panel.
